Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

LOCATION: Mandya | YEAR: 2023 | DECISION WEEK: 15
WEATHER CONTEXT:
Observed through 17-Oct: Pre-monsoon (Jan-May) rainfall 62mm. Kharif-to-date total: 451mm. Monthly distribution so far: [Jun: 50mm, Jul: 281mm, Aug: 35mm, Sep: 75mm, Oct: 10mm]. Longest dry spell so far: 23 consecutive days. Major storms so far: None.

RETRIEVED AGRONOMIC GUIDANCE (hybrid sparse+dense retrieval, top 3):
Ø The fertilizer containing nitrate such as CAN, ASN are more susceptible to loss of nitrogen through leaching and denitrification compared to ammonical form of nitrogen fertilizers containing no nitrate. Ø The use of nitrate fertilizers should therefore be avoided in paddy.
---
P-19 MPT 2. Assessment of avoidable yield losses due to major diseases of maize The avoidable yield loss trials were conducted using paired plot technique with ten replications under sick plot/ artificial epiphytotic conditions. The avoidable yield losses were recorded up to 10.6-31.9 per cent due to TLB (Bajaura, Rahuri, Dharwad), 31.43-37.12 per cent due to BLSB (Karnal, Kalyani) and 47.07 per cent due to FSR (Kalyani) (Table no. 10-15). MPT 3. Trap nursery trial for disease incidence The trap nursery trial was conducted to find out the occurrence of disease and/or any new disease on a set of susceptible maize inbred lines at Almora, Bajaura, Coimbatore, Delhi, Dharwad, Dhaulakuan, Dholi, Hyderabad, Imphal, Karnal, Kalyani, Ludhiana, Mandya, Pantnagar, Peddapuram, Rahuri and Udaipur locations (Table no. 16-32). MPT 4. Disease survey and surveillance in different maize growing areas Survey and surveillance were done in the mandate maize growing areas of Bajaura, Coimbatore, Dharwad, Dhaulakuan, Dholi, Hyderabad, Imphal, Kalyani, Karnal, Ludhiana, Mandya, Pantnagar, Peddapuram, Rahuri and Udaipur centres. During survey and surveillance of diseases, scoring was carried out along with the disease incidence in prescribed proforma (Table no. 33-47). MPT 5. Efficacy of fungicides/chemicals in management of maize diseases Evaluation of newer fungicides/ chemicals were undertaken at Kalyani, Pantnagar, Dharwad, Mandya and Dholi for the management of FSR; BLSB; Common rust; Polysora rust; and BLSB disease, respectively. The results revealed that foliar spray of Fluopyrum 21.37% w/w + Trifloxystrobin 21.37%
---

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen.
